q-37099.name: Question 1
q-37099.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x-x{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x-x{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =(2-{y}^{2})\,i-2xy\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t$ and $y=3{t}^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(2-9{t}^{4})\,i-6{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+6t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((2-9{t}^{4})\,i-6{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{t}\,i+6t\,j) \\  & =(2-9{t}^{4})\cdot \frac{1}{t}+(-6{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\cdot 6t \\  & =\frac{2}{t}-9{t}^{3}-36{t}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

q-37099.html:
Question 1
?

If f(x,y)=2x−xy2 and r(t)=ln⁡ti+3t2j, compute ddt[f(r(t))].

a
2t−3t−3tln⁡t
b
2t−3t2+36t3
c
2t−9t2−12t2ln⁡t
d
2t−9t3−36t3ln⁡t
e
2+9t3+6t3ln⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The chain rule in vector form states that ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y): ∇f(x,y)=∂∂x(2x−xy2)i+∂∂y(2x−xy2)j=(2−y2)i−2xyj

Next, we substitute x=ln⁡t and y=3t2 into the above to find ∇f(r(t)): ∇f(r(t))=(2−9t4)i−6t2ln⁡tj

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is r′(t)=ddt(ln⁡t)i+ddt(3t2)j=1ti+6tj.

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((2−9t4)i−6t2ln⁡tj)⋅(1ti+6tj)=(2−9t4)⋅1t+(−6t2ln⁡t)⋅6t=2t−9t3−36t3ln⁡t.

q-167407.name: Question 2
q-167407.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{xy})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{xy})\,j \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{y}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={t}^{3}$ and $y=t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}{2\sqrt{t}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{t}{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{t}{2}\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =\frac{3{t}^{2}}{2t}+\frac{t}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}t+\frac{1}{2}t \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡xy)\,j \\  & =\frac{y}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,i+\frac{x}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,i+\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,i+\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}+\frac{{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

If f(x,y)=arctan⁡xy and r(t)=eti+sin⁡tj, compute ddt[f(r(t))].

a
 et(cos⁡t+1)1+e2tsin2⁡t
b
et(sin⁡t+cos⁡t)1+e2tsin2⁡t
c
 et−cos⁡t1+e2tsin2⁡t
d
 et(sin⁡t+1)1+e2tsin2⁡t
e
 sin⁡t+et1+e2tsin2⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The chain rule in vector form states that

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y):

∇f(x,y)=∂∂x(arctan⁡xy)i+∂∂y(arctan⁡xy)j=y1+x2y2i+x1+x2y2j 

Next, we substitute x=et and y=sin⁡t into the above to find ∇f(r(t)):

∇f(r(t))=sin⁡t1+e2tsin2⁡ti+et1+e2tsin2⁡tj

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is

r′(t)=ddt(et)i+ddt(sin⁡t)j=eti+cos⁡tj.

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(sin⁡t1+e2tsin2⁡ti+et1+e2tsin2⁡tj)⋅(eti+cos⁡tj)=etsin⁡t1+e2tsin2⁡t+etcos⁡t1+e2tsin2⁡t=et(sin⁡t+cos⁡t)1+e2tsin2⁡t.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i-\,j.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

If f(x,y)=ex−y and r(t)=t2i−tj, compute ddt[f(r(t))].

a
(t+1)et2−t
b
t2et2−t
c
(2t+1)et2+t
d
2tet2+t
e
(t−2)et2+t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The chain rule in vector form states that

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y):

∇f(x,y)=∂∂xex−yi+∂∂yex−yj=ex−yi−ex−yj

Next, we substitute x=t2 and y=−t into the above to find ∇f(r(t)):

∇f(r(t))=et2+ti−et2+tj

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is

r′(t)=ddt(t2)i+ddt(−t)j=2ti−j.

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(et2+ti−et2+tj)⋅(2ti−j)=et2+t⋅2t+(−et2+t)⋅(−1)=(2t+1)et2+t.

q-95068.name: Question 5
q-95068.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})\,j \\  & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,i+\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y=t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,i+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,i+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i+j) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}+t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95068.html:
Question 5
?

If f(x,y)=x2+y2 and r(t)=eti+tj, compute ddt[f(r(t))].

a
t2et+t
b
e2tet+t
c
et+t2e2t+t2
d
e2t+te2t+t2
e
e2t−t2e2t+t2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The chain rule in vector form states that

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y):

∇f(x,y)=∂∂x(x2+y2)i+∂∂y(x2+y2)j=xx2+y2i+yx2+y2j 

Next, we substitute x=et and y=t into the above to find ∇f(r(t)):

∇f(r(t))=ete2t+t2i+te2t+t2j

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is

r′(t)=ddt(et)i+ddt(t)j=eti+j.

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ete2t+t2i+te2t+t2j)⋅(eti+j)=e2te2t+t2+te2t+t2=e2t+te2t+t2.

q-95086.name: Question 6
q-95086.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,k \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)\,i+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,j+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t+1,$ $y=2t$ and $z={t}^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,j+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,i+2\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,j+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,k)\cdot (\,i+2\,j+2t\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 1+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 2+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 2t \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2t(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)(1+t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

∇f(x,y,z)=∂∂x(xsin⁡(y+z))i+∂∂y(xsin⁡(y+z))j+∂∂z(xsin⁡(y+z))k=sin⁡(y+z)i+xcos⁡(y+z)j+xcos⁡(y+z)k

Next, we substitute x=t+1, y=2t and z=t2 into the above to find ∇f(r(t)):

∇f(r(t))=sin⁡(2t+t2)i+(t+1)cos⁡(2t+t2)j+(t+1)cos⁡(2t+t2)k

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is

q-95142.name: Question 7
q-95142.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}[x({y}^{2}-{z}^{2})]\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}[x({y}^{2}-{z}^{2})]\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}[x({y}^{2}-{z}^{2})]\,k \\  & =({y}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,i+2xy\,j-2xz\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t,$ $y=t+1$ and $z=t-1$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =[(t+1)^{2}-(t-1)^{2}]i+2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot (t+1)\,j-2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot (t-1)\,k \\  & =4t\,i+2(t+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,j-2(t-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+\,j+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(4t\,i+2(t+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,j-2(t-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,k)\cdot (\frac{1}{t}\,i+\,j+\,k) \\  & =4t\cdot \frac{1}{t}+2(t+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot 1-2(t-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot 1 \\  & =4+2(t+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t-2(t-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\  & =4+4\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

q-95074.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,k \\  & =2x\,i+2y\,j+4z\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t+1,$ $y=t-1$ and $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2(t+1)\,i+2(t-1)\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =i+j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2(t+1)\,i+2(t-1)\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k)\cdot (i+j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k) \\  & =2(t+1)\cdot 1+2(t-1)\cdot 1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =2t+2+2t-2+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =4(t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

If f(x,y,z)=x2+y2+2z2 and r(t)=(t+1)i+(t−1)j+sin⁡tk, compute ddt[f(r(t))].

a
2(t2−1)+cos⁡t
b
4(t+sin⁡tcos⁡t)
c
 2(2t2−sin⁡t)
d
 2sin⁡2t
e
 t(1+sin⁡tcos⁡t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The chain rule in vector form states that

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y,z):

∇f(x,y,z)=∂∂x(x2+y2+2z2)i+∂∂y(x2+y2+2z2)j+∂∂z(x2+y2+2z2)k=2xi+2yj+4zk

Next, we substitute x=t+1, y=t−1 and z=sin⁡t into the above to find ∇f(r(t)):

∇f(r(t))=2(t+1)i+2(t−1)j+4sin⁡tk

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is r′(t)=ddt(t+1)i+ddt(t−1)j+ddt(sin⁡t)k=i+j+cos⁡tk.

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2(t+1)i+2(t−1)j+4sin⁡tk)⋅(i+j+cos⁡tk)=2(t+1)⋅1+2(t−1)⋅1+4sin⁡t⋅cos⁡t=2t+2+2t−2+4sin⁡tcos⁡t=4(t+sin⁡tcos⁡t).

q-95149.name: Question 9
q-95149.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)+{e}^{y})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)+{e}^{y})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)+{e}^{y})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\,i+{e}^{y}\,j+\frac{1}{z}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,y={t}^{2},$ and $z=\frac{1}{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+{e}^{{t}^{2}}\,j+t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2t\,j-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+{e}^{{t}^{2}}\,j+t\,k)\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2t\,j-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,k) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}+2t{e}^{{t}^{2}}-\frac{t}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡t+2t{e}^{{t}^{2}}-\frac{1}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95143.name: Question 10
q-95143.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z)\,k \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,i-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,j+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,k \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,i-\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,j+\operatorname{cot}⁡z\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,$ $y={t}^{2}$ and $z={e}^{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cot}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{tan}⁡{t}^{2}\,j+\operatorname{cot}⁡{e}^{t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,k \\  & =i+2t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{cot}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{tan}⁡{t}^{2}\,j+\operatorname{cot}⁡{e}^{t}\,k)\cdot (i+2t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡t-2t\operatorname{tan}⁡{t}^{2}+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cot}⁡{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i+x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=\frac{t}{2}$ and $y=t$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\frac{t}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\frac{t}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2}\,i+j) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\frac{t}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(\frac{\pi }{2}))] & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In addition, we've been given that ∇f(x,y)=sin⁡yi+xcos⁡yj.

First, we substitute x=t2 and y=t into ∇f(x,y) to find ∇f(r(t)): ∇f(r(t))=sin⁡ti+t2cos⁡tj.

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is r′(t)=ddt(t2)i+ddt(t)j=12i+j.

Applying the chain rule, we get ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(sin⁡ti+t2cos⁡tj)⋅(12i+j)=sin⁡t⋅12+t2cos⁡t⋅1=12(sin⁡t+tcos⁡t).

q-94871.name: Question 12
q-94871.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=y{e}^{xy}\,i+(x{e}^{xy}+2y)\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=t+1$ and $y=t-1$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(t-1){e}^{(t+1)(t-1)}\,i+((t+1){e}^{(t+1)(t-1)}+2(t-1))\,j \\  & =(t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}\,i+((t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,j \\  & =i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}\,i+((t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2)\,j)\cdot (i+j) \\  & =(t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}\cdot 1+((t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2)\cdot 1 \\  & =(t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+(t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2 \\  & =2t{e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=-1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(-1))] & =2(-1){e}^{(-1)^{2}-1}+2(-1)-2 \\  & =-2-2-2 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

q-36215.name: Question 13
q-36215.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3y}\,i+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+3y}\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=t$ and $y={t}^{2}$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{2(t)}{(t)^{2}+3({t}^{2})}\,i+\frac{3}{(t)^{2}+3({t}^{2})}\,j \\  & =\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+3{t}^{2}}\,i+\frac{3}{{t}^{2}+3{t}^{2}}\,j \\  & =\frac{2t}{4{t}^{2}}\,i+\frac{3}{4{t}^{2}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{3}{4{t}^{2}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{3}{4{t}^{2}}\,j)\cdot (i+2t\,j) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2t})\cdot 1+(\frac{3}{4{t}^{2}})\cdot 2t \\  & =\frac{1}{2t}+\frac{3}{2t} \\  & =\frac{4}{2t} \\  & =\frac{2}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =\frac{2}{1}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-167498.name: Question 14
q-167498.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=2x{e}^{{x}^{2}+y}\,i+{e}^{{x}^{2}+y}\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡t$ and $y=t+{cos}^{2}⁡t$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{e}^{{sin}^{2}⁡t+t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,i+{e}^{{sin}^{2}⁡t+t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,j \\  & =2{e}^{t+1}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+{e}^{t+1}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+(1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2{e}^{t+1}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+{e}^{t+1}\,j)\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+(1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j) \\  & =2{e}^{t+1}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+{e}^{t+1}\cdot (1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =2{e}^{t+1}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{e}^{t+1}-2{e}^{t+1}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & ={e}^{t+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=-1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(-1))] & ={e}^{-1+1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2})\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+\frac{1}{2}j.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =({t}^{3/2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+\frac{1}{2}j) \\  & ={t}^{3/2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2}.\end{aligned}

$$

q-94885.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+y)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,3t⟩$ at the point $t=1.$
q-94885.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+y)),\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+y))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{1+(x+y)^{2}},\frac{1}{1+(x+y)^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=2t$ and $y=3t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨\frac{1}{1+(2t+3t)^{2}},\frac{1}{1+(2t+3t)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{1+(5t)^{2}},\frac{1}{1+(5t)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{1+25{t}^{2}},\frac{1}{1+25{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{1+25{t}^{2}},\frac{1}{1+25{t}^{2}}⟩\cdot ⟨2,3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+25{t}^{2}}\cdot 2+\frac{1}{1+25{t}^{2}}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{5}{1+25{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =\frac{5}{1+25(1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{1+25} \\  & =\frac{5}{26}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-167499.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{x}{y}$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,\sqrt{t}⟩$ at the point $t=9.$
q-167499.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y}),\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=2t$ and $y=\sqrt{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},-2⟩\cdot ⟨2,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\cdot 2-2\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=9$ is

$$

q-94888.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{z}^{2}+{y}^{3}),\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{z}^{2}+{y}^{3}),\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{z}^{2}+{y}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨{z}^{2},3{y}^{2},2xz⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,$ $y=4$ and $z=\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨(\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3})^{2},3(4)^{2},2t\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}-3,48,2t\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}-3,48,2t\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}⟩\cdot ⟨1,0,\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}}⟩ \\  & =({t}^{2}-3)\cdot 1+48\cdot 0+2t\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}\cdot \frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}-3}} \\  & ={t}^{2}-3+0+2{t}^{2} \\  & =3{t}^{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(2))] & =3(2)^{2}-3 \\  & =12-3 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t-1,$ $y=3$ and $z=2t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨\frac{2(t-1)}{(t-1)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2t)^{2}},\frac{2(3)}{(t-1)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2t)^{2}},\frac{2(2t)}{(t-1)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2t)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{6}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{4t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),2t⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{2t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{6}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{4t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}⟩\cdot ⟨1,0,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{2t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}\cdot 1+\frac{6}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}\cdot 0+\frac{4t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2t-2+8t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10} \\  & =\frac{10t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(0))] & =\frac{10(0)-2}{5(0)^{2}-2(0)+10} \\  & =\frac{-2}{10} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the rate of change of the function f(x,y,z)=ln⁡(x2+y2+z2) with respect to t along the curve r(t)=⟨t−1,3,2t⟩ at the point t=0.

Correct
EXPLANATION

The rate of change of f(x,y,z) with respect to t along the curve r(t) is given by ddt[f(r(t))]. To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y): ∇f(x,y)=⟨∂∂x(ln⁡(x2+y2+z2)),∂∂y(ln⁡(x2+y2+z2)),∂∂z(ln⁡(x2+y2+z2))⟩=⟨2xx2+y2+z2,2yx2+y2+z2,2zx2+y2+z2⟩

Next, we substitute x=t−1, y=3 and z=2t into the above to find ∇f(r(t)): ∇f(r(t))=⟨2(t−1)(t−1)2+(3)2+(2t)2,2(3)(t−1)2+(3)2+(2t)2,2(2t)(t−1)2+(3)2+(2t)2⟩=⟨2t−25t2−2t+10,65t2−2t+10,4t5t2−2t+10⟩

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is r′(t)=⟨ddt(t−1),ddt(3),2t⟩=⟨1,0,2⟩.

Applying the chain rule, we get ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=⟨2t−25t2−2t+10,65t2−2t+10,4t5t2−2t+10⟩⋅⟨1,0,2⟩=2t−25t2−2t+10⋅1+65t2−2t+10⋅0+4t5t2−2t+10⋅2=2t−2+8t5t2−2t+10=10t−25t2−2t+10.

Therefore, the rate of change of f along the curve r(t) at t=0 is ddt[f(r(0))]=10(0)−25(0)2−2(0)+10=−210=−15.
